finalMessage:
I linked `deploy/network.tf` to C-TLS-ONLY. No tests cover it.

**Tests:** None. `deploy/` has no test coverage, and the README says no test runs there. The only verification that names C-TLS-ONLY is V-INFRA-REVIEW, a manual per-release review by a second engineer. Nothing in `src/` references the item or the file.

**The change:** I added one line to C-TLS-ONLY in `trace/threats.yaml`:

```yaml
    code: [deploy/network.tf]
```

It is a file-level link. ostf can't resolve Terraform resource symbols (`deploy/network.tf#aws_lb_listener.https` gives UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE), so the file is the finest target it can take. `ostf context deploy/network.tf` now shows `implements C-TLS-ONLY`. I did not edit `deploy/network.tf` or the item's text.

**`ostf check --base main`:** passes with no errors. The only message is an info line about R-ORDER-NOTE and R-VOLUME-DISCOUNT having no links, which was already there before my change.

**Items in this change:**
- **C-TLS-ONLY** is marked `risk-relevant: ask before changing`. My change touches it, since I added a link to the item. Its text is unchanged. I checked the file against the claim: port 443 uses `ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06`, which permits only TLS 1.2 and 1.3, and port 80 returns a 301 redirect to HTTPS. So the item is still true. Please have another principal review this change in the pull request, per the policy. If you would rather I hold off on touching a risk-relevant item, I can revert the line.
- **THREAT-EAVESDROP**, which C-TLS-ONLY controls, is unchanged.
- **V-INFRA-REVIEW**, which verifies C-TLS-ONLY, is unchanged.

Nothing is committed.
